units.translation: You do not see these things, but I do.
I have not seen the race of this company.
But see these blows, and whence they come upon the heart.
Seeing this company of the land.
Seeing him who never boasted, subdued by helpless miseries.
Seeing these advocates of my mother.
I see great gain for these citizens.
Hear well, having seen what is just.
But nowhere would you see the same wing of toil.
I see a throng shaded with freshly cut branches, bowing down.
So that they may see the proof of this arrival.
May I never again see the water that brings bride-price.
Do not love violent things (Hermann reads στέρξης [may you love]) seeing them with unjust eyes.
Having seen the device of wings.
You see Justice voiceless, unseen by one sleeping, walking, and sitting.
For if I shall see only one who guards the hearth (Wellauer reads ψόλον [smoke]).
You will see the form of no mortal.
But never yet did I see such a clear vision.
May he see an unharmed escape.
See, powerful curses of the dead, see the remnants of the Atreidae.
See the double tyranny of the land.
See the offspring bereft of the eagle father.
I tremble to see the blood-bringing deaths.
I see this man obtaining what he deserves.
What penalty do you see being in it?
May I see my enemies thus luxuriating.
And no one has ever seen Zeus defeated.
We see the Aegean sea blooming with corpses.
I saw the city of Ilium faring as it fared.
It is possible to see this man fallen.
Whom may I ever see dead.
Seeing these young birds seated on the tomb.
I see this nurse of Orestes weeping.
I see a man hated by the gods holding his seat at the navel.
I have seen before the painted women bringing food to Phineus.
And now you see these mad women captured.
And I see all these things trampled underfoot.
May you not see me dragged from the seats of the many gods.
And Zeus pities you, seeing you helpless.
May you never see me, O revered Fates, becoming the bride of Zeus's bed.
For I do not see how I might escape the counsel of Zeus.
And now you see me, how I am prepared – I sit as a suppliant.
See what I, a god, suffer at the hands of the gods.
Let him look upon mortal insolence.
And to keep away the unseen wrath of my father from the altars.
Nor among the goddesses seen by the gods.
These things have long been seen and planned.
see! (imperative), may I see, I may see, to see, having seen
may he see with a kindly eye
the prudent things are good for those who seek them
